AC EVIDENCE, verified against merged main (Gerrit 2097).

AC1 the scan exists and passes: test_the_fit_then_wire_derivation_has_exactly_one_body walks every *.py under src/rebar except the owner outbound_comments.py, parses each with ast, and reports any FUNCTION whose body calls both a fit and to_wire. 2 passed.

AC2 conjunction, not a single token: the matcher requires _FIT_CALLS (fit_comment / sanitize_comment / fit_preserving_marker) AND _WIRE_CALL (to_wire) in the SAME function scope. Both halves are load-bearing and this was found empirically, not assumed - a FILE-level conjunction false-positives on the Data Center adapter, which contains both atoms for unrelated reasons (to_wire on the description field at :107, fit_comment as its Backend-port implementation at :331). They never meet in one body. Matching either atom alone would fire on innocent reconciler modules, and a guard that cries wolf gets deleted. It currently reports exactly two sites: the owner's fit_for_send and the Cloud adapter's add_comment.

AC3 reasonless marker rejected: test_the_one_legitimate_second_fit_is_marked_with_a_reason asserts the owner-side marker carries a non-empty reason, and directly asserts that '# comment-fit-ok: defensive' has a reason while a bare '# comment-fit-ok:' does not. Passing.

AC4 mutation evidence, three runs, each applied to live code in src/rebar/_store/hlc.py and reverted:
  (a) unmarked copy - appended _sneaky_fit_then_wire() calling sanitizer.fit_comment(body) then codec.to_wire(fitted). Result: FAILED, 'the fit-then-wire derivation was re-implemented outside _engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py'.
  (b) same copy with '# comment-fit-ok: probe' on the fit line. Result: 1 passed.
  (c) same copy with a bare reasonless '# comment-fit-ok:'. Result: FAILED again.
Restored; working tree clean; full file 22 passed.

Also recorded: my first draft of the marker regex omitted re.MULTILINE, so '$' matched only at end-of-file and the owner-marker assertion failed against whole-file text. The test caught it. That is the second time this session I made that exact slip (the 111a guard was the first).
